description: The Scotland Heat Map is a Scottish Government GIS resource that estimates heat demand for every property in Scotland, to help plan the reduction of carbon emissions from heating buildings. It combines data sources held by the Scottish Government into property- and area-level heat demand estimates, and adds existing and planned heat networks and existing and potential energy supply so users can see who needs heat and where it could come from. Each estimate has a confidence level from 1 to 5, higher where building type, age and floor area are known; gridded layers give average confidence at 50, 250 and 500 metre resolution for all of Scotland. The latest edition, Scotland Heat Map 2022, was released to local authorities in November 2023. Access: a public interactive website and GeoTIFF grids linked from data.gov.uk; the detailed dataset is shared through data sharing agreements. Licence: the public site grants a revocable, view-only, non-commercial licence under Crown copyright; the grids' catalogue records state no licence. Caveats: demand is modelled, not metered, and reliability varies. Simulation uses are heat network zoning, local heat and energy efficiency strategies and building decarbonisation scenarios. Related records: EPC registers and national building stock models.
